independent_computation.question: For the coupled scenario whose two named coupling sources are Black Cleaver (Carve) and Bloodsong (Spellblade / Expose Weakness), is the correct per-event precision label for the disputed event 'exact' (authored absolute timestamp) or 'hit' (position defined by a hit in the attack sequence)?
independent_computation.step_1_trigger_predicate_from_wiki: S1 defines the Bloodsong event by a hit predicate, not a clock: the bonus 100% base AD physical damage is delivered by 'your next basic attack within 10 seconds' after an ability, and it is explicitly an [[on-hit]] instance. The 10 s is a *window in which the trigger may occur*, not a timestamp. The coupling debuff inherits the same anchor: Expose Weakness (8% melee / 5% ranged increased damage from all sources, 4 s) has a 1.5 s cooldown that 'starts after using the empowered attack' — i.e. the amp window opens at a hit, not at a cast time.
independent_computation.step_2_second_coupling_source_is_also_hi: S2 defines Carve per damage instance ('Dealing physical damage … applies a stack'), capped for non-basic damage at once per frame. The shred state is therefore a function of the hit count, and is frame/hit-quantized by the game's own rule — there is no continuous-time law that fixes it.
independent_computation.step_3_resolve_the_hit_to_a_time: S5 gives the only timing law available for such an event: swings occur on the deterministic grid t_i = i·Δ, Δ = 1/(AS·u). 'Next basic attack after the cast' therefore resolves to t_k for the integer k = min{i : t_i ≥ t_cast}. The event's position is determined *up to the swing grid* — the sources supply the hit index, the model supplies the grid. That is hit precision by construction; nothing in either wiki text authors an absolute timestamp for this event.

step_4_numeric_demonstration_that_the_st.formula: mean Carve stacks over h hits = C − C(C−1)/(2h), C = 5 (S6); armor reduction = 6% per stack, cap 30% (S2)
step_4_numeric_demonstration_that_the_st.reading: Two fights of the same wall-clock length but different AS·u land different shred (18% vs 27%), because the state advances per hit. The mitigation an event sees is therefore keyed by hit ordinal, not by clock time — the same conclusion the Bloodsong trigger predicate forces.

independent_computation.step_5_the_project_standard_forbids_the_: S3 is the engine's own documented convention for exactly this family: spellblade-carried extra on-hits are 'attributed to a prefix of autos, not the spellblade's actual weave times'. An event whose placement is an attribution to a hit prefix does not carry an authored timestamp, and S4 states the corpus rule that an approximation is 'never silently presented as exact'. S7 confirms the codebase reserves 'exact' for events with AUTHORED EVENT TIMING (a sourced timestamp: cast time, proc trigger, or buff window). A Spellblade/Carve on-hit event has a sourced *trigger*, not a sourced *time*.
independent_computation.conclusion: The disputed event is a hit-carried item event in a scenario whose only two coupling sources (Carve, Spellblade/Expose Weakness) are both defined by hit predicates in the cached wiki text. The sourced precision key is the hit, so 'hit' is correct and the previous 'exact' over-claimed a timestamp precision no source supplies.

confidence_and_limits.confidence: high on direction (the sources define both coupling effects by hit predicates; the old label asserts a precision no source supports), medium on the enum's full membership
limits: The `event_precision` enum is defined in src/, which this runbook forbids reading; the verdict is a judgment between the two given labels on the evidence, not a re-derivation of the enum.

The golden baseline (scripts/golden_baseline.json) is out of bounds, so events[82] could not be identified by name — the identification rests on the scenario id naming its two coupling sources, both of which are hit-triggered.

If the enum's 'exact' were ever intended to mean 'exactly resolved on the deterministic grid' rather than 'authored absolute timestamp', 'hit' is still the strictly more informative and equally true label; it is not wrong under either reading, whereas 'exact' is wrong under the S7 reading.
